Insect growth regulators (IGRs) comprise a group of compounds classified
by the United States Environmental Protection Agency as “biochemical”
pesticides. One such IGR that is widely used for stored tobacco and tobacco
Products is methoprene, the active ingredient of Kabat and Dianex. These

products offer unique control of the cigarette beetle (las ioderma sercome) and
the tobacco moth (Ephistia ) by disrupting the life cycles of these

insects. Methoprene is not acutely toxic to insects or animals, and even has
FOA clearance for use in potable water.

Methoprene is normally applied to tobacco at the parts per million level.
fenltories of methoprene residues is desirable to ensure appropriate and
economical application rates and efficacy of control. Chromatographic methods
for analysis of methoprene residues date back to 1976. For example, a
mode-switching HPLC approach was disclosed by one of us (R. A. Heckman, Tobacco
Chemists’ Research Conference, Atlanta, GA) fn 1984. This procedure involved a
semi-preparative normal phase separation, followed by a reversed-phase end
analysis. This approach was highly successful in that methoprene and an
internal standard, MPM (the secondary buty! ester homologue), appeared as the
major peaks in the resulting reversed-phase chromatogram. The method was also
capable of accurate quantitation at the fractional parts per million level.

However, routine sample throughput for this approach was 12-15 samples per
week for one analyst - too low for the current level of monftoring.
Consequently, a new procedure for analysis of methoprene residues on tobacco
was developed that is based on the Varian AASP (Advanced Automated Sample
Processor). The new method requires only 0.5 g of ground tobacco or dust and
21) glassware and plasticware items are disposable. The extraction is
performed in a Centrex Microfilter using hexane. Following centrifugation, an
aliquot is passed through an aminopropy! bonded phase cartridge where
methoprene and HPM are retained. These materials are then eluted directly onto
a silica cartridge using hexane - methylene chloride. Residual solvent is
largely removed by passage of dry nitrogen through the cartridge for several
minutes, The resulting normal phase cartridges are then presented (in
cassettes of 10) to the AASP which functions much like an autosampler using a
Vista 402 Chromatography Oata System. Final determination is made in a
reversed-phase mode using a C18 colum and UV detection. Thus, the new
procedure substitutes two solid-phase adsorption steps in place of the
semi-preparative HPLC step fn the former method. With this approach,
approximately 40 samples can be prepared for automated HPLC analysis in a

‘ normal work day.

WASHINGTON (AP) -- The Supreme Court today let stand a ruling
that shields cigarette makers from any legal liability for
aliegedly failing to warn adequately about the dangers of smoking.

The justices, without comment, refused to review a federal
appeals court ruling that such legal claims are preempted by
federal law.

The court thus steered clear of a still-pending lawsuit against
three cigarette manufacturers by a Little Ferry, N.J., woman who
died of lung cancer.

Rose Cipollone smoked for 40 years before quitting in 1982,
after her right lung was removed. She died in 1984 but her husband,
Antonio, continued her 1983 products liability lawsuit.

The lawsuit names as defendants Liggett Group Inc., Philip
Morris Inc. and Loew's Theatres Inc., which owns Lorillard.

The suit alleged, among other things, that the three
manufacturers are liable for Mrs. Cipollone'’s death because they
failed to warn adequately about the health hazards of cigarette use
and because they undermined the effectiveness of health warnings
later required by federal law.

‘The Federal Cigarette Labeling and Advertising Act requires all
cigarette packages and cigarette advertising to contain health
warnings.

The first warning, required in 1966, said “Caution: Cigarette
Smoking May Be Hazardous To Your Health.” In 1970, the warning was
amended to read, "Warning: The Surgeon General Has Determined That
Cigarette Smoking Is Dangerous To Your Health."

The act was amended in 198$ to provide four rotational warnings.

based on smoking and health shall be imposed under state law with

PHILIP MORRIS U.S.A. SAYS NEW STUDY MERITS CAREFUL REVIEW

NEW YORK, October 18, 1996 ~ We are thoroughly reviewing what may
be a significant study published in the October 18 issue of the journal Science.
Based on what we have seen so far, the research is extremely interesting and
merits careful review.

While statistical studies have shown that cigarette smoking is a risk factor
for lung cancer, this study appears to suggest that at the molecular level
benzofa}pyrene, a chemical found whenever any organic substance is burned,
may, under certain circumstances, be involved in the mechanism that leads to
lung cancer. We look forward to learning more about this and other research in
an attempt to understand what mechanisms may be at work.

From a legal and regulatory perspective, this research does not change the
fact that smoking is an informed choice that people have made and, we believe,
will continue to want to make. Our success in the litigation has been due, in
large part, to the fact that the public has been fully aware of the claims that
smoking causes lung cancer. The research reported today and the media
attention being given to it are consistent with our long-held position that the
mechanism by which a cell becomes cancerous is a complex process not yet
explained. This research may provide insights into aspects of this process.

Charles Sydnor, Ph D., is president and chief executive officer of Central Virginia

continued his teaching career as a visiting professor of history at Vanderbilt University in Nashville, Tenn,
in the summer of 1974 and as an assistant to an associate professor at Longwood College in Farmville,
Va., from 1972 to 1980,

In 1975, Sydnor began a nine-year association with public television -- working as an independent
project producer and writer for WCVE-TV (PBS), one of the stations operated by the CVETC in
Richmond, Va. Over these years, he produced several documentaries, including the award-wincing “Adolf

president of Hampton-Sydney College in Hampton-Sydacy, Va. He left this position in 1982 to work as

Va., in 1984. He served in this office until accepting his current position at CVETC, An expert on the
history of Nazi Germany and the Holocaust, Sydnor also bas worked for the Department of Justice since

analysis and modeling. Before joining The Sapphire Group™ , Dr. Graves was Washington,

consultant group that analyzed water and air quality data for the Council on Environmental

international public affairs program supporting a controversial new product

dangers to corporate America of the initiative and referendum process.

RE: Dr. M. H. Bilimoria

Dear Derick:

Confirming our telephone conversation in early July, in my judg-
ment, the Bilimoris/Ecobichon projects with reference to “studies on
ambient tobacco smoke" and on the “usefulness of the micro-nucleus
test", should be rejected because they are unimaginative proposals
without good scientific foundations, and, in addition, have a number
of political pitfalls. However, the most important reason for my recom
mending their rejection is the scientific worthlessness of the project.

‘There has been « tremendous literature on the alleged relationships
between carcinogenic activity and aryl hydrocarbon hydroxylase (AM).
‘The consensus at the present time is that this reaction is not a good
indicator or predictor for carcinogenic activity. Furthermore, all
animal models tried to date are unsuitable for simulating the alleged
effects of smoking on human smokers, and even more unsuitable for simu-
lating "passive smoking" in man. This applies particularly to rats.
This is shown, for example, in a very recent paper by $. K. Loscutoff
et al, and A. P. Wehner, entitled “Dosimetry and Cardiopulmonary Punction
in Rats Chronically Exposed to Cigarette Smoke", ‘Toxicology Appl.
Pharm.’ 64 (2): 335-352 (June 30, 1982), which demonstrates and refers
to previous literature showing that the smoke taken in is in complete
Gisequilibrium with reference to gas phase, particulate phase, etc., as
compared to smoke taken in by human ssokers. Any results which would be
obtained by Bilimoria, regardless whether favorable or unfavorable from
our point of view, would be meaningless.

Similar reasonings apply to the micronucleus test as a biological
Bonitor of tobacco emke exposure. Cigarette smoke has been shown many
times to be mutagenic. It has also been shown, even by those who very
strongly believe in mutagenesis tests, that such tests, at best, have a
qualitative significance and are quantitatively meaningless. I personally
hold an exceedingly dim view of even the qualitative usefulness of such
tests. Adding another test to those already reported in the literature,
is, in my judgment, total waste.

I have been informed that Dr. Fagan of Philip Morris has advised
your counterpart in Canada by telephone about a month ago, or earlier,

that he considers the Bilimoria projects worth]. Dr. Fagan has $

writing. , *
